_meta.description: Cumulative DOM/CSS selector catalog built by the qa-ticket-verify skill. Keys are dotted paths '<area>.<elementName>'. Before adding a selector, check it isn't already here under a different name. Prefer the most specific already-verified selector; only add a new one when nothing close enough exists yet.
_meta.howToExtend: When a needed selector is missing: 1) search the PR diff for the exact data-testid/aria-label/id being added or touched, 2) grep the existing frontend/legacy source for the component, 3) as a last resort inspect the live page via Playwright's snapshot tool and note the accessible name/role instead of a brittle CSS path. Always record where it came from in 'source'.
_meta.playwrightMcpNote: browser_click/browser_type's `target` accepts either a snapshot ref (e.g. 'e21', no 'ref=' prefix) or a raw CSS selector string directly — verified during the MON-207985 run. For anything inside the legacy iframe, Playwright resolves it via iframe[name="main-content"].contentFrame() automatically when given a selector; browser_evaluate needs an explicit document.querySelector('#main-content').contentDocument instead.
_meta.conventions: '${placeholder}' in a selector means it's a template — substitute the real value described in the adjacent note. A value ending in ' (text-match)' means it's not a CSS selector but a cy.contains()-style text match; use Playwright's text/role-based lookup for those instead of a raw selector. getByLabel({label,tag}) resolves to '${tag}[aria-label="${label}"]'; getByTestId({tag,testId}) resolves to '${tag}[data-testid="${testId}"]' (tag defaults to any element when omitted) — both are project Cypress commands (packages/js-config/cypress/e2e/commands.ts), not real selectors themselves.
_meta.coverage: Extracted from centreon/tests/e2e/features/** across all 28 top-level feature directories (146 feature files) via parallel agent sweep, plus live verification during the MON-207985 dry run. Legacy pages render inside iframe #main-content (see generic-legacy-iframe); React pages use data-testid/aria-label directly on the top-level document.
